Synopsis:
    Fitch Ratings warns that rising Japanese bond yields — with 10Y JGBs hitting 3% for the first time since 1996 — may incentivise domestic institutional investors (megabanks, life insurers, GPIF) to repatriate capital from foreign assets back into Japanese debt. Fitch expects the BOJ to hike rates faster than market consensus in 2026-2027, supporting the yen and domestic real rates, thereby reducing the appeal of lower-yielding foreign investments.

Q01. Is the content's main message about EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
Relevance: NO — The article is entirely focused on Japanese monetary policy, JGB yields, and domestic capital allocation by Japanese institutional investors. No reference to EU energy or German power markets.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 35 — The BOJ tightening direction is broadly known; however, Fitch's specific call that the BOJ will hike faster than consensus in 2026-2027, combined with the GPIF repatriation risk flagged in July, adds a moderately incremental layer of uncertainty around the pace and scale of capital repatriation.
